saints.name: St. Robert of Newminster
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: An English Cistercian abbot of gentle rule and great austerity, friend of the hermit St. Godric…
biography: Born at Gargrave in Yorkshire about 1100, Robert is said to have studied at Paris before serving as rector of his native village, and then entered the Benedictine abbey of Saint Mary in York. In 1132 he was among the monks expelled from York who, on land given by Archbishop Thurstan, founded Fountains Abbey in the valley of the Skell, which soon joined the Cistercian reform.

About 1138 he led a colony from Fountains into Northumberland, where Ranulf de Merlay and his wife Juliana gave land near Morpeth for a new house. As first abbot of Newminster he ruled for twenty-one years, and from it sent out monks to found Pipewell in 1143, Roche in 1147, and Sawley in 1148.

Remembered for austerity, gentleness, and a gift of prophecy, he was the close friend of the hermit Godric of Finchale, who is said to have seen Robert's soul carried up to heaven on the night of his death. Robert died at Newminster on 7 June 1159, and his tomb in the abbey church became a place of pilgrimage.
saints.knownFor: First abbot of Newminster; Cistercian holiness.
